title: The Body in Flow
coreMove: Turn bodily sensation into skilled involvement by giving the body rhythm, challenge, control, and trained attention.
sourcePressure: The body becomes a flow arena through movement, disciplined control, sex handled tastefully, yoga, martial arts, seeing, music, and taste, all organized by skill and attention rather than mere stimulation.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reduce the body chapter to fitness motivation, indulgence, or wellness slogans.

sourceAnchors.name: yoga and the martial arts
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen heading index calls yoga and the martial arts the ultimate control
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Yoga and martial arts make the point cleanly: the body becomes absorbing when control is practiced one breath, stance, and correction at a time.

sourceAnchors.name: the flow of music
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen heading index names music as a bodily and sensory flow channel
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Music enters through the ear, but the work is bodily too: timing, breath, pressure, and attention learn to move together.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a physical therapist restarting a patient's walking practice
exampleSpecs.audience: rehab patients and clinicians who need challenge without punishment
exampleSpecs.stakes: too much difficulty risks pain, too little gives no involvement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places two tape marks on the clinic floor and asks the patient to choose the stride target that is reachable but not automatic
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The blue tape line curls at one corner of the clinic floor

exampleSpecs.domain: a community choir singer learning breath control
exampleSpecs.audience: adults who think music is passive listening unless they perform professionally
exampleSpecs.stakes: he may quit because he cannot hear progress yet
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the flat first rehearsal beside the night he tracks one breath cue through the same phrase and hears the line hold
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Lars nearly left the choir after the second rehearsal

exampleSpecs.domain: a chef training her palate for acidity
exampleSpecs.audience: people who consume taste but rarely train attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: a sauce will fail service unless she can detect the imbalance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her mentor asks which cup has one extra drop of vinegar, and Olivia must predict before seeing the labels
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Tell me which cup changed," the sous-chef says

exampleSpecs.domain: a beginner aikido student learning a fall
exampleSpecs.audience: learners who confuse bodily control with force
exampleSpecs.stakes: a stiff landing could injure him and end the class early
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mat is quiet, and Matteo loosens his shoulder, rolls once, then uses the impact sound as feedback for the next attempt
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The dojo mat holds the print of bare feet

exampleSpecs.domain: a photographer training sight during a dull commute
exampleSpecs.audience: creative hobbyists who wait for inspiration
exampleSpecs.stakes: the commute can be dead time or a practice in seeing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you stand on the tram platform and choose one color reflection to track instead of letting the whole street blur
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are early for the tram and the pavement is still wet

exampleSpecs.domain: a partner planning a non-graphic intimacy conversation around attention and presence
exampleSpecs.audience: couples who confuse closeness with automatic chemistry
exampleSpecs.stakes: the relationship needs care without turning the lesson into performance pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: ask what would change if the goal were shared attention rather than outcome, then show Devon putting the phone away and naming one boundary
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes when closeness is treated as attention, not conquest?

skillTargets: using rhythm and feedback in movement

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one ordinary bodily act, walking, stretching, tasting, or listening, and give it one precise cue to track for sixty seconds.
